title: The Treaty of Lancaster, 1744: how Virginia claimed Kentucky
summary: At Lancaster, Pennsylvania, in 1744 the Six Nations gave Virginia a deed to the lands of its colony for goods and £200 in gold. Virginia read it as reaching the Mississippi; the Iroquois said they had sold only to the Alleghenies.
bodyMarkdown:
The treaty made at Lancaster, Pennsylvania, in the summer of 1744 was negotiated hundreds of miles from Kentucky, but it became one of the paper foundations of Virginia's claim to the land.

## A council in a courthouse

From late June into early July 1744, [about 250 Iroquois delegates](https://grokipedia.com/page/Conrad_Weiser) led by Canassatego of the Onondaga met colonial commissioners in the [court house at Lancaster](https://worldhistorycommons.org/excerpts-treaty-lancaster-1744). [Onondaga, Oneida, Cayuga, Seneca and Tuscarora](https://www.wvencyclopedia.org/entries/736) leaders attended. Virginia sent [Thomas Lee](https://grokipedia.com/page/Thomas_Lee_%28Virginia_colonist%29) and William Beverley, Maryland and Pennsylvania sent their own men, and Conrad Weiser interpreted.

The quarrel was over the colonies' western edges. The Six Nations claimed the backcountry by right of conquest, won in the [Beaver Wars](/stories/iroquois-beaver-wars/) of the previous century. When Maryland pointed to more than a hundred years of possession, Canassatego answered: ["what is one hundred years in comparison to the length of Time since our Claim began?"](https://worldhistorycommons.org/excerpts-treaty-lancaster-1744) He complained of "that Pen and Ink work that is going on at the Table," pointing at the secretaries.

With Virginia, the Iroquois speaker Tachanoontia called the Six Nations' claim "a Right too dearly Purchas'd, and which cost us too much Blood" to give up. He insisted that if Virginians settled the backcountry, "our Warriors Marching that way to the Southward" must share in what they planted. Those war parties were bound for southern enemies such as the [Catawba](/stories/the-catawba-and-the-northern-war-parties/).

Virginia answered with a conquest story of its own: "the Great King holds Virginia by Right of Conquest, and the Bounds of that Conquest to the Westward is the Great Sea."

## Gold on the table

On July 2 the Virginians laid out goods "and Two hundred Pounds in Gold." They offered them on one condition: that the Six Nations "immediately make a Deed, recognizing the King's Right to all the Lands that are or shall be by his Majesty's Appointment in the Colony of Virginia." The chiefs put their marks and seals to it, and Canassatego delivered it for the Great King.

A Six Nations speaker had already put the bargain in plain words: "What little we had for the Land goes soon away, but the Land lasts forever."

## Two readings of one deed

The deed's wording mattered because Virginia's charter of 1609 granted it land running [from sea to sea](https://www.virginiaplaces.org/settleland/ohio.html). The Virginia commissioners came home believing they held a deed for [everything west to the Mississippi River and north to the Great Lakes](https://www.wvencyclopedia.org/entries/736). The Iroquois believed they had sold only the land between the Blue Ridge and the Allegheny Mountains. Within a year, Virginia had [granted 300,000 acres](https://worldhistorycommons.org/excerpts-treaty-lancaster-1744) of western land to colonists.

The argument followed the land west. At [Logstown in 1752](/stories/treaty-of-logstown-1752/) Virginia asked the Six Nations to confirm the Lancaster deed, and the Seneca leader Tanacharison at first said the sale had reached no farther than the Alleghenies. The Iroquois finally gave up their claim between the Ohio and Tennessee rivers at [Fort Stanwix in 1768](/stories/treaty-of-fort-stanwix-1768/). Through all of it the [Shawnee, Cherokee and other nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Six_Nations_land_cessions) who held much of that country by possession kept their own claims.

## Kentucky today

The treaty has no Kentucky place to pin. It was made in Pennsylvania, and the Lancaster courthouse site is [now occupied by the Soldiers and Sailors Monument](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Six_Nations_land_cessions). When Virginia created [Kentucky County](https://grokipedia.com/page/Kentucky_County,_Virginia) on December 31, 1776, it treated its western frontier as reaching the Mississippi, as its charter claimed. The Lancaster deed was one of the papers behind that claim.
